about: The MAC a portal is addressed by, and the serial a box derives from it.
notes: Arguments are the helper's name and its argument: normalizeMac, isMacAddress or serialFor.

serialFor is not a secret and not a security measure. Some portals check that the serial and the MAC agree, so it is derived rather than random: the same MAC must always present the same box, which is what a portal pinning a session to a device expects. An implementation deriving it differently gets a handshake refused with no useful error.

cases.name: a MAC already in the usual form is unchanged
no separators at all are accepted
cases.why: People paste a MAC out of a panel in whatever form it was shown.

cases.name: something that is not twelve hex digits is handed back as typed
cases.why: Upper-cased and trimmed, but not reshaped: the caller shows it to the user, and silently reformatting a typo makes it harder to see.

cases.name: so is one with no separators
the serial is the last thirteen hex digits
separators make no difference to it
a shorter value is padded to thirteen
and it is always upper case
